input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: § 28.1 imposes Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — a jurisdiction outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) with exclusive foreign venue, i.e. walk-away territory, and it directly conflicts with § 28.2, which already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County with only a customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out (which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum). The shortest complete cure is to change the governing law in § 28.1 to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore forum words, leaving § 28.2 untouched so the preferred venue element remains met.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
mappings.quote: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Replace Singapore governing law and exclusive Singapore forum in § 28.1 with New York law, leaving § 28.2's exclusive New York County forum intact.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced Singapore law and the exclusive Singapore forum with New York law, which is our accepted position and removes the conflict with § 28.2's exclusive New York County jurisdiction (Delaware, California or England and Wales with London courts would be an acceptable fallback).
